methodological_rigor.justification: This is a prospective, single-arm, multicenter phase II study (n=30) comparing outcomes to historical Interfant-06 controls. The absence of a concurrent control arm is acknowledged as a limitation driven by the prohibitive poor outcomes of Interfant-06, making randomization ethically challenging. The historical comparison uses 214 selected controls with individually matched analysis as a sensitivity check. PK analysis is straightforward with appropriate CL calculations. The small sample size (n=30) and non-randomized design limit statistical power and causal inference. The historical control comparison may be confounded by evolving supportive care practices. All patients completed the full blinatumomab course, suggesting good protocol adherence.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: KMT2A-rearranged infant ALL is one of the highest-risk leukemia subtypes in pediatrics, with prior 4-year DFS of 44% on Interfant-06. The current study shows 4-year DFS of 83.3% and OS of 93.3%—a striking improvement. This finding is particularly compelling given that it represents sustained benefit beyond the historically defined 2-year high-risk recurrence window. The FDA approval of blinatumomab from age 1 month (2024) and the ongoing Interfant-21 and COG AALL2321 trials both build on this work. The clinical relevance is exceptional given the disease severity, and the PK data supporting no dose adjustment for infants have direct clinical utility.

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript reports key survival endpoints with 95% CIs, cumulative incidence of relapse, infection data by treatment phase, and PK parameters with comparison to historical values. The data supplement provides detailed patient characteristics, statistical methods, and infection tables. The ethics approval and consent processes are documented. The comparison with historical controls using both selected cohort and individually matched analysis adds robustness. Raw data are not publicly shared. The absence of adverse event data from the historical Interfant-06 comparison for infectious mortality (different classification systems) is appropriately acknowledged.

novelty_literature.justification: This is the first study to demonstrate long-term (4-year) durable benefit of upfront blinatumomab in infant KMT2A-r ALL, extending previously published 2-year results. The finding that no further events occurred between the 2-year and 4-year follow-up is novel and clinically important for demonstrating sustained remission beyond the historical high-risk relapse window. The PK characterization confirming comparable clearance in infants versus older children supports dosing guidance for this age group. This is a proof-of-concept milestone for a paradigm shift in infant ALL treatment.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is concise and clearly organized as an update to a previously published primary analysis. The survival figures with both single-arm and comparative data are clear. The infection characterization by treatment phase (Fig 2) is informative. The PK table (Table 1) appropriately contextualizes infant data against older age groups. Limitations are honestly disclosed. The discussion appropriately flags ongoing trials (Interfant-21, AALL2321) for prospective validation. Minor weakness: the short manuscript format leaves limited space for the nuances of the historical comparison methodology.

key_strengths: Striking and durable improvement in 4-year DFS (83% vs 44%) and OS (93% vs 60%) compared with historical Interfant-06 controls in one of the highest-risk pediatric leukemia subtypes
Sustained benefit demonstrated beyond the 2-year historical relapse window with no new events between 2 and 4-year follow-up
Zero infection-related fatalities postinduction compared with 4% in Interfant-06, despite intensive immunosuppression from blinatumomab plus chemotherapy
PK data confirming comparable blinatumomab clearance in infants vs older children, supporting current FDA-approved dosing from age 1 month
key_concerns: Small sample size (n=30) in a single-arm study with historical controls; randomized validation is needed and ongoing
Historical control comparison may be confounded by improved supportive care practices over time, potentially overestimating the blinatumomab benefit
63% of patients required IVIg administration, suggesting substantial B-cell aplasia burden that is not fully characterized in terms of duration and infectious consequences
HSCT in 11 of 30 patients (37%) may confound the survival analysis; the relative contributions of blinatumomab and transplant to outcomes cannot be separated in this design
chief_reviewer.rationale: This 4-year long-term follow-up of an infant KMT2A-r ALL blinatumomab study demonstrates exceptional and durable benefit in one of the most challenging pediatric leukemia settings. Despite the inherent limitations of a small single-arm study with historical controls, the magnitude of the survival difference and the clinical context support Tier 2 placement, with minor revisions needed to better address the HSCT confounding and IVIg burden characterization.
